title: Let Every Ear Attend
description: Let Every Ear Attend in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 53.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let ev-ery ear at-tend And ev-ery heart re-joice; The trum-pet of the Gos-pel sounds With an in-vit-ing voice.

lines: The trumpet of the Gospel sounds
And vainly strive with earthly toys
Ho! ye that pant for streams
Here you may quench your raging thirst
Like floods of milk and wine.
Lord, we are come to seek supplies

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
